title: AMRaCut: Scalable Partitioning for Adaptive Mesh Refinement
problem: Mesh partitioning for distributed PDE solvers faces trade-offs between partition quality and parallel scalability. Traditional methods (spatial ordering, multi-level graph partitioning) don't scale efficiently for AMR workloads with dynamic mesh evolution.
motivation: Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR) is critical for efficient PDE solvers but dynamic mesh evolution creates partitioning challenges. Scalable partitioning with high quality is needed to maintain HPC efficiency.
method: AMRaCut: Distributed-parallel mesh partitioner using parallel label propagation and graph diffusion. Operates mostly locally on initial partitions, limiting inter-process communication to neighboring processes. Leverages AMR's property of mostly local changes.
key_novelty: Parallel label propagation approach for mesh partitioning; graph diffusion for locality; efficient handling of dynamic AMR mesh evolution; balanced communication-quality trade-off.
contributions: AMRaCut partitioner with parallel label propagation and graph diffusion
Efficiency comparable to space-filling curve methods
Maximum partition load within 2x of optimal
Validation on Finite Element SpMV workloads
limitations: Load imbalance of 2x may impact some applications; locality-based approach may not suit non-AMR workloads; initial partition quality affects final result.
